Title: Adnex bags Bursa building refurbishment job
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Adnex Group Bhd's wholly owned unit Adnex Interior Solution Sdn Bhd has secured a contract from Bursa Malaysia Bhd for refurbishment works at its Exchange Square main building.
Adnex said the RM14.19 million contract,  accepted on Oct 2, covers refurbishment works at levels six, 14 and 15 of the building.
The works are expected to take three months and are targeted for completion in the fourth quarter of 2026.
Adnex said the contract would support efforts to secure new projects and expand its order book, which would contribute to the group's revenue and earnings.
Managing director Adrian Kan Wai Chun said the latest contract was the second purchase order Adnex had received from Bursa Malaysia, following refurbishment works at the Exchange Square public listing gallery earlier this year.
"Upon completion of this refurbishment work, this further reaffirm our competitiveness to undertake larger scale of interior-fit-out project with more than RM14 million value per project project within a short delivery period, and yet required to comply with all the stringent and necessary compliance laws and regulations," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Petronas Chemicals appoints Izwan Ismail as MD, CEO effective Jan 1, 2027
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Petronas Chemicals Group Bhd (PetChem) has appointed Izwan Ismail as managing director (MD) and chief executive officer (CEO) effective Jan 1, 2027.
In a filing with Bursa Malaysia, the petrochemical producer said the appointment was approved at a special meeting held today.
The board of directors, at the meeting, noted the resignation of Mazuin Ismail as MD and CEO effective the same date following his retirement from the Petronas group, it said in a separate filing.
PetChem said Izwan, 51, brings over 29 years of experience spanning finance, corporate planning, strategy, commercial management, operations and technology.
"Since October 2024, he has served as vice president, group technology and commercialisation, where he leads Petronas Nasional Bhd's (Petronas) transformation of its artificial intelligence (AI) and digital ecosystem, as well as its research and development ecosystem.
"Currently he serves as director of Petronas Gas Bhd and various subsidiaries of the Petronas Group," it said.
Izwan began his career with Arthur Andersen in Sydney in 1997 before joining Petronas in 2000, where he served in corporate finance, group accounts and group treasury at its subsidiary, MISC Bhd.
He holds a Bachelor of Commerce with a double major in Accounting and Information Systems from the University of New South Wales, Australia, and a Master of Business Administration from Harvard Business School, United States.
"He is a fellow of Chartered Accountants Australia & New Zealand (CA ANZ) and a member of the Malaysian Institute Of Certified Public Accountants (MICPA) and Malaysian Institute of Accountants (MIA)," it added.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Jobbie, Lotus's target RM20,000 for Makna
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysian peanut butter brand Jobbie and Lotus's Malaysia are expanding their breast health awareness campaign.
RM1 from every limited-edition jar sold will go to the National Cancer Society of Malaysia (Makna).
The campaign, running from Oct 1 to Dec 31, involves 20,000 specially designed jars, targeting RM20,000 in contributions to support cancer patients.
The initiative, dubbed the Pink Wobbly Breast Odyssey, follows Jobbie's first collaboration with Makna in 2024, which involved 5,000 jars.
The campaign jars feature illustrations and information on common breast cancer signs and symptoms, aiming to encourage conversations about breast health at home.
Jobbie Sdn Bhd chief executive officer Victor Chin said the campaign was partly inspired by his personal experience, after his mother was diagnosed with breast cancer when he was about 10.
Although she survived, she continued to undergo regular check-ups decades later, he said.
"The key thing is about reaching 20,000 families," Chin said, adding that men should also take a more active role in supporting women in their lives.
The campaign will be available at 71 Lotus's outlets nationwide.
Lotus's Malaysia corporate services director Azliza Baizura Azmel said the retailer's nationwide store network could help make breast health conversations more accessible.
Makna head of division Nisha Sanita said the funds would assist cancer patients, particularly those facing financial constraints.
The campaign also features content creator Chin Pui Ting, known as Dead Pudds, who shared her experience of supporting her mother through cancer.
As part of the campaign, Makna's Awareness Truck will be stationed at IOI City Mall from Oct 2-4, offering augmented and virtual reality experiences.
Free breast health consultations and risk assessments will also be available during the three-day activation.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Air quality improves nationwide, no unhealthy readings
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Air quality improved nationwide amid transboundary haze, with no areas recording unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 5.30pm today.
According to the Department of Environment's (DoE) Air Pollutant Index Management System (APIMS), 65 areas recorded moderate air quality, while three were in the good category.
This marked an improvement from 9.20am, when
Sri Manjung in Perak
was the only area nationwide with an unhealthy API reading, at 108.
Sri Manjung's API had fallen to 92 by 5.30pm, placing it back in the moderate category.
Cheras in Kuala Lumpur recorded the highest API reading at 96, followed by Sri Manjung, Sri Aman and Serian in Sarawak, each at 92.
Other areas with relatively higher readings included Seberang Perai (89), Seberang Jaya (81) and Minden (80) in Penang.
In Perak, Tasek Ipoh recorded 89 and Pegoh, Ipoh, 85, while Samarahan (88) and Kuching (84) were among the higher readings in Sarawak.
Batu Muda in Kuala Lumpur recorded 86, while Pasir Gudang (82) and Larkin (80) recorded the highest readings in Johor.
In Sabah, Tawau recorded 81, while Sungai Petani in Kedah recorded 80.
Several areas that had recorded elevated readings during the haze episode also showed improvement, including Nilai, Negri Sembilan (79); Shah Alam (78), Klang (70) and Johan Setia (64) in Selangor; and Putrajaya (73).
Meanwhile, three areas recorded good air quality — Limbang in Sarawak (43), Politeknik Kota Kinabalu (40) and Kota Kinabalu (29) in Sabah.
API readings of between zero and 50 are classified as good, 51 to 100 as moderate, 101 to 200 as unhealthy, 201 to 300 as very unhealthy, and above 300 as hazardous.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Zetrix AI tumbles 33pct, closes at 11 sen
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Zetrix AI Bhd shares plunged 33 per cent on Friday, closing at 12 sen after a report said the company owes the government more than RM200 million in unremitted collections.
The counter fell 5.5 sen from Thursday's close of 16.5 sen, after opening at 16.5 sen and touching an intraday low of 10 sen.
It was the most actively traded stock on Bursa Malaysia, with about 922 million shares changing hands.
The selloff followed a Straits Times report that Zetrix AI owes the Road Transport Department (RTD) more than RM200 million in road tax, driving licence renewal fees and traffic summonses collected since the start of its three-year contract in May 2023.
The Transport Ministry subsequently confirmed the outstanding amount.
Zetrix AI, formerly known as MyEG Services Bhd, was a pioneer in providing online government services through its link-up with RTD.
The stock has come under sustained selling pressure since Aug 28, when it plunged 50 per cent to 29.5 sen amid heavy trading.
It has remained among Bursa Malaysia's most actively traded counters in the weeks since.
The latest selloff brings its decline from the year's peak of 89.5 sen on April 21 to about 88 per cent, while its market capitalisation has fallen sharply from levels earlier this year.
The sustained pressure has also reduced managing director Wong Thean Soon's stake.
His interest fell from more than 30 per cent at the end of August to 10.6 per cent as of Thursday, according to the company's latest disclosures.
Separately, Zetrix AI announced on Monday that its external auditor, TGS TW PLT, had resigned, citing portfolio rationalisation and resource management. The group said it would announce a new auditor in due course.
The company reported a net profit of RM269.3 million for the second quarter ended June 30, bringing first-half net profit to RM540.58 million.
Meanwhile, RTD said on Friday that Zetrix AI and My E.G. Sdn Bhd will be suspended as its collection agents from 12.01am on Oct 5.
The suspension covers RTD services previously offered through MYEG, including road tax and driving licence renewals and summons-related services.
RTD said its services would continue through its official and alternative channels.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Lee had space to speak, but did not use it, says PKR deputy sec-gen
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Former Petaling Jaya member of parliament Lee Chean Chung had the opportunity to voice his views within PKR but did not attend most of the party's central leadership council meetings since November.
PKR deputy secretary-general Bryan Ng said the MPP was one of the party's main forums, attended by its president Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and other leaders, including ministers and deputy ministers.
"Various national issues, government policies and current affairs are raised and discussed at these meetings.
"Party leaders have the opportunity to ask questions, give their views, disagree and raise issues directly with the top leadership," he said in a statement.
He said Lee, who was elected to the MPP, later chose to resign from the party leadership council.
Ng also disputed Lee's claim that he was unable to raise issues affecting Petaling Jaya, saying Lee had been invited to meetings on flood mitigation by the Petaling Jaya City Council (MBPJ) and at state level, but did not attend most of them.
He said Lee was also invited to meetings on the Petaling Jaya Local Plan, which covers land use, traffic, public facilities and future development, but again did not attend most of the meetings.
"If there is a question, ask. If you disagree, debate. If there is a better proposal, put it forward," he said.
Ng said Lee had previously raised his views on the proposed separation of the attorney-general and public prosecutor roles, with the government later making improvements to the proposal.
He also questioned Lee's decision to remain with PKR while attending programmes and appearing on platforms organised by Parti Bersama Malaysia, saying disciplinary action against members who supported or assisted political opponents was not unusual.
Lee's resignation as Petaling Jaya MP
took effect today
following his meeting with Dewan Rakyat Speaker Tan Sri Johari Abdul yesterday.
Lee said that he had received a decision from PKR on Sept 30 to suspend his party membership for three years.
He claimed the suspension was linked to his outspoken stance on various issues affecting the public, saying it had also left him unable to voice his position within the party.
Ng said the people wanted representatives who were present, worked with relevant agencies, followed up and sought solutions.
"An effective member of parliament is not merely someone who issues statements.
"Their responsibility is to bring issues to the relevant authorities, attend meetings, push for action and follow up until a solution is reached.
"That is what the people have the right to expect from every politician. I wish him all the best in his journey ahead," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: PSD awaits Home Ministry probe before deciding on MCBA DG viral incident
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Public Service Department (PSD) will await the outcome of the Home Ministry's investigation before deciding on the next course of action over a viral incident involving Datuk Seri Mohd Shuhaily Mohd Zain.
Its director-general Tan Sri Dr Wan Ahmad Dahlan Abdul Aziz said the department had yet to receive any report against the Malaysia Border Control and Protection Agency director-general over his actions in the viral clip showing him berating two men.
"So far, the department has yet to receive any report on the viral issue involving the MCBA director-general.
"I believe the Home Ministry, which is responsible for MCBA, is conducting an investigation.
"As such, I need to wait because I cannot say what is right or wrong without clear facts," he said when met at the Santuni Pesara programme here today.
It was reported yesterday that a clip had gone viral showing a man believed to be Shuhaily berating two men, with one of them appearing to have been grabbed forcefully by the ears.
Besides the video, a copy of a police report allegedly lodged by the individual who was purportedly subjected to rough treatment by Shuhaily also went viral.
Shuhaily said at a press conference yesterday that he was prepared to be
investigated
over the incident.
He also said that he was prepared to accept any decision made regarding the matter.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 155 firefighters, 12 assets deployed for Bahrain F1 Grand Prix in Malaysia
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: A total of 155 Fire and Rescue Department personnel and 12 assets have been mobilised to ensure emergency and rescue preparedness throughout the Gulf Air Bahrain Formula 1 (F1) Grand Prix at the Sepang International Circuit (SIC).
In a statement, the department said the deployment would cover the three-day event from today until Oct 4, with personnel and assets stationed at strategic locations to ensure emergencies could be handled swiftly and effectively.
"Among the assets deployed are a Fire Rescue Tender (FRT), two Compact Fire Rescue Tenders (CFRT), a 10,000-litre water tanker, three Emergency Medical Rescue Services (EMRS) ambulances and four department buses.
"An A109E helicopter has also been stationed at SIC to support monitoring, emergency response and rescue operations when required," it said.
The department said 153 firefighters and officers, comprising fire marshals, medical teams and medevac personnel, had been assigned to the circuit as part of the overall preparedness operation.
Fire and Rescue Department director-general Datuk Seri Nor Hisham Mohammad said the deployment reflected the department's commitment to supporting international events while prioritising safety and emergency preparedness.
"The department is always prepared to provide support for large-scale events, particularly those involving large crowds as well as participants and delegations from Malaysia and abroad.
"The deployment of officers, personnel and assets at strategic locations is to ensure that any emergency and rescue needs can be handled quickly, systematically and effectively," he said.
Hisham said coordination between the department, organisers and other relevant agencies had also been strengthened to maintain the required level of operational preparedness throughout the event.
"The safety of spectators, participants, personnel and everyone involved is our priority, and the department will ensure that every deployment is carried out in accordance with established standard operating procedures," he said.
The event marks the return of Formula 1 racing to Sepang after Malaysia last hosted the race in 2017.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Johor-Singapore RTS Link passenger service to start in February 2027
Article:
JOHOR BARU: Passenger service on the Johor Baru-Singapore Rapid Transit System (RTS) Link is expected to begin in February 2027, with all system tests and trial runs targeted for completion by Dec 31.
RTS Operations Pte Ltd (RTSO) said in a statement today that the timeline took into account the expected duration of the remaining works, as well as the time required for third-party safety certification and approvals from the grantors of both countries.
"Our goal is to provide a safe and reliable service on the RTS Link," it said.
The RTS Link, a bilateral project between Malaysia and Singapore, will connect Bukit Chagar in Johor Baru with Woodlands North in Singapore.
Upon completion, the service will have a peak capacity of up to 10,000 passengers per hour in each direction, with the journey between the two stations expected to take about 5 minutes.
Co-located Customs, Immigration and Quarantine (CIQ) facilities will be provided at both Bukit Chagar and Woodlands North stations, allowing commuters to clear immigration at their point of departure.
RTSO said the project was expected to significantly improve cross-border connectivity and facilitate daily travel between Johor Baru and Singapore.
It said the RTS Link was also expected to strengthen people-to-people ties and generate shared economic and social benefits for both countries.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Mark your calendars: Syed Saddiq, Bella invite all to wedding receptions
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Muar member of parliament Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman and artiste Bella Astillah have invited the public to their wedding receptions in Muar, Johor, and Kota Kinabalu, Sabah.
The receptions will be held on Oct 25 and 31 respectively.
"We hope to celebrate our union with as many people as possible, and that's why we decided to have this 'kenduri rakyat'," Syed Saddiq said.
The receptions will follow their solemnisation ceremony, which will take place on Oct 10.

Title: Masseur gets 20 months' jail, two strokes for molesting customer
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: A masseur who molested a male customer during a massage was sentenced to 20 months in jail and two strokes of the rotan by the magistrate's court here today.
Magistrate Marilyn Kelvin sentenced Ahmad Johan Yong Abdullah @ Yong Kui Fook, 31, after he pleaded guilty to the charge.
According to the charge, Johan used criminal force against the victim with the intention of outraging his modesty at a massage and reflexology centre in a shopping mall here around 1.30pm on June 21.
He was charged under Section 354 of the Penal Code, which carries a jail term of up to 10 years, or a fine, or whipping, or any two of the punishments, upon conviction.
According to the facts of the case,Johan repeatedly touched the victim inappropriately despite being told to stop.
The victim, who felt uncomfortable with Johan's actions, subsequently lodged a police report.
Johan, who was unrepresented, pleaded for leniency, while Deputy Public Prosecutor Ronny Antony urged the court to impose a deterrent sentence.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: RTD suspends MYEG, Zetrix as collection agents from Oct 5
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Road Transport Department (RTD) will suspend the services of My E.G. Sdn Bhd and Zetrix AI Bhd, both under the MYEG Group, as its collection agents effective Oct 5.
RTD director-general Datuk Aedy Fadly Ramli said the decision was made after taking into consideration compliance with the terms and conditions of the agreement, as well as outstanding obligations that had yet to be fulfilled or resolved by the companies.
"RTD would like to inform that the services of My E.G. Sdn Bhd and Zetrix AI Bhd under the MYEG Group as collection agents on behalf of RTD will be suspended effective 12.01am, Oct 5," he said in a statement today.
Following the suspension, all RTD services previously offered through MYEG Group channels will also be suspended from Oct 5.
However, Aedy said RTD services would continue as usual through its official and alternative channels.
For motor vehicle licence (LKM) renewals, motorists can use RTD counters, the MyJPJ application, RTD Public Portal, RTD kiosks, RTD Mobile counters, Pos Malaysia outlets and Puspakom for private and commercial vehicles in the de-controlled category.
For Malaysian driving licence (CDL) renewals, the available channels are RTD counters, MyJPJ, RTD Public Portal, RTD kiosks, RTD Mobile counters and Pos Malaysia outlets.
Applications for Malaysian Learner Driving Licences (LDL) can be made through RTD counters, MyJPJ, RTD Public Portal, RTD kiosks and RTD Mobile counters.
For summons checks and payments, the public can use RTD counters, MyJPJ, RTD Public Portal, RTD kiosks and RTD Mobile counters.
For ownership transfers, services are available at RTD counters and RTD kiosks for private individual motorcycle transactions involving Malaysian citizens. The RTD Public Portal is available for private individual and company transactions, while eAuto companies can be used through the Temporary Ownership Transfer System and eSerahan Ownership Transfer.
Aedy said bookings for the Computerised Law Test (KPP01) already made through MYEG before Oct 5 could proceed as usual.
"However, for new bookings made from Oct 5, the booking and implementation of the test must be conducted through KPP Test Centres provided at driving institutes nationwide," he said.
For summons payments involving non-Malaysian citizens at Malaysia-Singapore border entry points, payment facilities will be provided through RTD Mobile Units stationed at the Sultan Abu Bakar Complex (KSAB) and Sultan Iskandar Building (BSI) in Johor.
The facilities will operate from 8am to 10pm.
Aedy also advised the public to use the official channels provided to ensure transactions could be carried out smoothly and securely.
"RTD remains committed to ensuring continuity in the delivery of services to the public and ensuring that every transaction is carried out in an orderly, transparent and with integrity."
The suspension comes after the Transport Ministry separately confirmed to business news portal The Edge that Zetrix AI
owes the government
more than RM200 million in unremitted collections.
The amount involves money collected from customers for vehicle road tax renewals, driving licence renewals and traffic summonses.
The Straits Times, citing official documents, reported that the unremitted collections dated from the start of Zetrix AI's 3-year contract with RTD in May 2023.
Zetrix AI was formerly known as MYEG Services Bhd.
The company has provided online government services, including those linked to RTD, since 2000.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Damai Perdana residents seek official safety assurance after landslide
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Residents of Pangsapuri Damai Perdana 2 have demanded an official explanation from management and local authorities regarding building safety, following a notice allowing them to return home starting today.
The dilemma stems from resident concerns over a clause stating that returning to the premises is at their own risk, raising doubts about safety a week after a landslide occurred nearby.
Block D resident Lina Ridzuan, 43, said the permission letter issued by the local authority lacked concrete safety guarantees and basic utility restoration.
"The local authority handed us permission letters to return, but what disappointed residents is the 'at own risk' clause. An answer like this only reinforces suspicions that the area is not entirely safe.
"If a follow-up soil settlement occurs and threatens lives, who will be held responsible? We want a solid answer and guarantee, not a hands-off decision," she said when met today.
Lina expressed frustration over the Joint Management Body (JMB), claiming it had failed to appear or provide official updates since the soil movement occurred last week.
She added that the absence of management and local community leaders left residents feeling abandoned and torn over what to do.
"Since the day of the incident, there has been no official information from our Joint Management Body. When told to return today, water supply was still unavailable.
"No maintenance or repair work is visible at the site. How can elderly residents and families with many children haul belongings up to upper floors?" she said.
Another Block D resident, Anun Sharif, 74, said she was too terrified by the incident to move back into her home for now.
Anun decided to stay at her child's house nearby after the incident, returning only occasionally to inspect her unit.
"During the incident around 8pm, neighbours felt tremors and saw water flowing. Even though there is a letter allowing us back today, I remain worried about safety aspects and fear the worst.
"To make matters worse, water supply to Blocks C and D has been cut off for a week. At my age, I do not have the strength to carry buckets of water from the tanks provided and have to rely on my children," she said.
Water supply is expected to be restored by Oct 10, complicating daily affairs for residents instructed to return earlier.
"I hope the relevant authorities and apartment management take swift action by coming to the ground to give an official safety guarantee," she said.
It was previously reported that residents living near the slope at Pangsapuri Damai Perdana in Cheras were
ordered to evacuate
following a landslide near the building.
Selangor Fire and Rescue Department operations assistant director Ashrul Riezal Asbar said the department received an emergency call at 9.03pm regarding the incident near Block D of Pangsapuri Damai Perdana.
The landslide is believed to have been caused by an underground water pipe leak.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 14-year-old teenager sexually assaulted by man at PPR
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A 14-year-old teenager was sexually assaulted by a man at a People's Housing Project flat in Cheras.
Cheras deputy police chief Superintendent Lim Chun How said the case came to light following a report lodged by the teenager's mother on Sept 29.
He said the suspect is a man in his 40s.
"Police confirm receiving a report from the victim's mother concerning the sexual assault of her son.
"The case is being investigated by the Kuala Lumpur police Sexual, Women and Child Investigation Division (D11)," Lim said in a statement today.
It is understood that the victim knew the suspect and claimed to have been assaulted on several occasions.
The victim's mother lodged a police report after her son confided in her.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Keep fighting until final whistle, Anwar tells Harimau Malaya
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has called on the Harimau Malaya squad to maintain its winning momentum in the Fifa Asean Cup 2026 third-place playoff on Monday.
In a Facebook post today, Anwar said the fighting spirit and determination shown by the national squad throughout the campaign remained a source of pride for Malaysians despite missing out on the final.
He also congratulated Harimau Malaya on its emphatic 6-0 victory over Singapore last night.
"The fight is not over. The focus is now on the third-place playoff. Maintain the momentum, fight until the final whistle and bring home a victory for Malaysia!
"Although we missed out on the final, the fighting spirit and determination shown by Harimau Malaya throughout the campaign remain a source of pride for all Malaysians, proving that the national team can compete and give their best," he said.
In their final Group A Division 1 match at Si Jalak Harupat Stadium in Bandung last night, Malaysia thrashed Singapore 6-0, but the result was not enough to take the national squad into the final.
Malaysia and Indonesia were tied on seven points and had the same goal difference of plus nine, but the advantage went to the Garuda squad, who scored 11 goals compared with Malaysia's nine.
Indonesia advanced to the final as group champions after thrashing Bangladesh 9-2 at Gelora Bung Karno Stadium (GBK) in Jakarta.
Malaysia will meet the Group B runners-up in the third-place playoff, most likely to be Vietnam, who now lie second in the group with their final match to be played this evening.
Both the third-place playoff and the final between Indonesia and Thailand will be held at GBK on Monday.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Physiotherapist recalls emotional moment beside grieving Dr M
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A physiotherapist who was seen crying beside Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad during his wife's funeral said he was deeply moved by the former prime minister's grief.
"Seeing Tun M (Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad) in such a state of sadness moved me so deeply that I shed tears," said Kevin Choo, 31.
Choo's presence beside Dr Mahathir during the funeral of his wife, Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohd Ali, on Monday drew attention on social media after he was seen crying alongside the former prime minister.
Sharing his experience, he said he had been providing physiotherapy treatment to the couple for the past two years.
"When I first started working with them, I felt a little shy and awkward because we all know who they are. But over time, we became more comfortable with each other.
"Despite their age, they remained determined to undergo physiotherapy to stay healthy," he said.
Kevin said that on the day of Dr Siti Hasmah's funeral, his role was to monitor Dr Mahathir's condition and assist him with his physical needs.
"As everyone knows, he was going through a tremendous loss. Although Tun M was in a wheelchair and required oxygen support, he still wanted to be there to pay his final respects to his wife.
"Personally, seeing him in that situation affected me deeply. It showed that behind the image of a prominent figure, he is also a husband who had lost the most important person in his life.
"As a healthcare worker, I tried to remain professional and focused on my duties. But in a situation like that, we are human too, and we have feelings," he said.
On the video of him crying beside Dr Mahathir that went viral, Choo said he did not expect his emotions to attract public attention.
"At the time, I was simply trying to carry out my duties as usual. Having known and been with them for several years, it was difficult to put those feelings into words.
"I tried to hold back my emotions, but the tears eventually came. I think anyone who was there could feel how heavy the atmosphere was.
"The loss of Dr Siti Hasmah also affected me personally. I had been with and known them for several years, so she was not merely someone I cared for as part of my job," he said.
Dr Siti Hasmah, 100, died at the National Heart Institute (IJN) in Kuala Lumpur at 9.20am on Monday.
She was buried at Pusara Negara in Precinct 20, Putrajaya, later that day.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: No media ban at Siti Hasmah grave visit, Media Club lodges police report over doctored photo
Article:
PUTRAJAYA: There was no official restriction or ban on media coverage when former prime minister Tun Dr Mahathir Mohamad visited the grave of his late wife, Tun Dr Siti Hasmah Mohamad Ali, at Pusara Negara here yesterday, says Putrajaya Media Club (KMP).
KMP said media personnel covering the visit were aware of their journalistic ethics and the need to respect human values, privacy and the family's sensitivities while carrying out their professional duties in a sombre setting.
"KMP wishes to stress that media personnel did not receive any official notification of restrictions or a ban on recording from Dr Mahathir's office or family at the location.
"Media practitioners on duty understand their responsibility to respect human values, privacy and the family's sensitivities, especially when reporting in a sombre setting," it said in a statement today.
KMP said the presence of media personnel at such locations was part of their professional responsibility to document important events of significance to society and the country.
The statement came after a social media account altered an image of a group of photographers and journalists covering Dr Mahathir's visit to Siti Hasmah's grave and replaced them with images of animals.
The image was accompanied by the caption, "Akal waras semakin sukar ditemui" (Sound minds are increasingly difficult to find), which KMP said was insulting to media personnel carrying out their professional duties.
"KMP understands the right of every individual to criticise, but freedom of expression should not be used as an excuse to demean or insult media personnel.
"Any criticism should be made based on the actual facts and context," it said.
KMP has lodged a report with the Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) and police, urging appropriate action to be taken against the account owner.
KMP said it would continue to defend the dignity, safety and rights of media personnel to perform their duties professionally without insults or personal attacks.
Meanwhile, Putrajaya district police chief assistant commissioner Aidi Sham Mohamed, when contacted by Bernama, confirmed receiving the report and said the case was being investigated under Section 505(c) of the Penal Code and Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998.
Earlier, social media users questioned the media and public taking photographs of Dr Mahathir during his visit to his wife's grave, describing the act as inappropriate.
KMP also expressed its condolences to Dr Mahathir and his family following Siti Hasmah's death, describing her passing as a great loss to her family, society and the country.
Siti Hasmah died at the National Heart Institute (IJN) on Monday at the age of 100. She is survived by 7 children.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Driver fined RM1,000 for using criminal force on sister's ex-boyfriend at nasi kandar shop
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: What began as a meeting to settle a misunderstanding between two men turned into a physical confrontation at a nasi kandar restaurant, ending with a personal driver being fined RM1,000 by the magistrate's court today.
Muhammad Zulhafiz Muhammad Zahari, 30, pleaded guilty to using criminal force against his sister's former boyfriend, 24-year-old parcel delivery man Muhammad Afiff Zahran Zori, without grave and sudden provocation.
Magistrate Amalina Johar fined Zulhafiz RM1,000 and ordered him to serve one month in jail if he failed to pay the fine.
The court heard that Afiff and Zulhafiz had met at 12.11am on July 15 at a restaurant in Taman Segambut Bahagia, Sentul, to resolve a misunderstanding between them.
However, the meeting turned heated when Zulhafiz accused Afiff of assaulting his sister.
Afiff denied the allegation, but the confrontation escalated when Zulhafiz and a friend allegedly pulled him, causing him to fall.
Zulhafiz then choked Afiff before the situation was brought under control by Afiff's family members and other diners.
He was then charged under Section 352 of the Penal Code, which provides for a maximum three-month jail term, a fine of up to RM1,000, or both upon conviction.
During mitigation, Zulhafiz, who represented himself, pleaded for the minimum fine, telling the court that he supported his elderly parents and his sister, who is still studying.
Deputy public prosecutor Amritpreet Kaur Randhawa urged the court to impose a proportionate sentence.

Title: Affordable housing to affordable living: Hopes for 2027 budget
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: For many Malaysians, affordability is no longer just about buying a home. It is about whether the home they can access, rented or owned, is one they can realistically afford to live in.
This distinction matters as the 2027 budget takes shape. The Ministry of Finance's Pre-Budget Statement places homeownership and rental affordability alongside public transport, urban liveability, and wider household cost pressures, from transport to healthcare, education, and childcare.
For the property sector, this shows why affordability needs to be measured differently. Where a home is located, how people get to work, how much they spend on transport and utilities, and whether they can access essential services all affect whether a home is truly affordable over time.
1. Recognising Rental Affordability as Part of Malaysia's Housing Agenda
Rental is an increasingly important part of how Malaysians navigate the housing market.
Recent PropertyGuru platform data shows rental searches outpacing sale searches, with rental properties also shortlisted more frequently than sale properties. This points to rental as a significant part of the property search journey, not simply a temporary step before ownership.
For many households, renting provides flexibility. This includes younger workers, those building financial capacity, people relocating for employment, and households prioritising proximity to workplaces or public transport.
However, rental affordability is not just about finding the lowest monthly rent. A young worker who rents further from the city may save on rent but spend more time and money commuting. A family may find a cheaper home but still struggle if schools, childcare, public transport, or healthcare are far away.
PropertyGuru's H1 2026 Consumer Sentiment Study adds to this picture. Among renters surveyed, 81% said rents were too high; 51 per cent had moved further from the city because of housing costs, and 89 per cent paid less than RM1,500 a month.
The National Housing Policy 2026–2035 also reflects this broader housing landscape, with rental affordability, secure tenancy, housing quality, and liveable neighbourhoods among its areas of focus.
The 2027 Budget is an opportunity to continue recognising rental as a core part of Malaysia's housing ecosystem. This includes improving access to a suitable, trusted and affordable rental supply while giving responsible landlords and agents clearer pathways to bring that supply into the market.
This is also the gap we are looking to support through Pay Per Post, our new flexible listing option for trusted agents and property owners. By making it easier to bring individual listings onto PropertyGuru and iProperty Malaysia, we hope to help more suitable rental supply reach renters where they are already searching, while keeping trust and listing quality central to the experience.
2. Looking Beyond Housing Price to the True Cost of Living
A lower rent or mortgage does not always mean a home is more affordable. If that home comes with a longer commute, higher transport costs, higher energy bills, or limited access to essential amenities, the total burden on the household may still be significant.
This is why affordability should also consider the recurring costs of living in a home.
Energy efficiency, public transport access, connectivity, climate resilience, and proximity to everyday services are not just lifestyle preferences. They influence what households spend every month and how practical a home is to live in.
PropertyGuru's H1 2026 Consumer Sentiment Study found that 86 per cent of respondents considered sustainable features important when buying or renting a home, while 78 per cent took climate risks such as flooding and landslides into account when purchasing property. Infrastructure and amenities were also prioritised by 30 per cent of respondents.
For the 2027 budget, this means housing affordability should be viewed alongside the wider cost of living in a particular location. A more practical measure of affordability would take into account not only rent or purchase price but also transport, utilities, connectivity, and access to essential services.
3. Using Demand-Led Data to Guide Housing and Infrastructure Planning
Housing needs differ by location, household type, income level, and stage of life. Planning works best when it reflects how people are actually searching, moving, and making trade-offs.
For policymakers and industry players, this means looking beyond headline supply numbers to understand local demand, rental and ownership intent, price accessibility, existing housing stock, and connectivity.
Public datasets remain essential, but they can be strengthened by complementary demand signals from the private sector, including how consumers search, shortlist, and enquire. Used responsibly and in aggregate, these signals can help identify mismatches earlier so that homes, infrastructure, and services are better aligned with community needs.
The 2027 Budget provides an opportunity to embed this demand-led approach more strongly in housing planning.
Towards Affordable Living
The housing market is not made up of one type of household or one housing pathway. Malaysians move between renting and ownership at different stages of life, depending on income, household needs, employment, and location.
This is why housing affordability should be treated as a question of affordable living. An affordable home is also about whether a household can manage the cost of living there. Rent or mortgage, transport, utilities, maintenance, and access to everyday needs all play a part.
As Malaysia shapes the 2027 Budget, bringing homeownership, rental, connectivity, infrastructure, and liveability into the same conversation would move housing policy closer to how Malaysians actually live, move, and make decisions today.
============
Vic Sithasanan is managing director at PropertyGuru Malaysia & iProperty Malaysia

Title: Ravindran: Lift SST on residential security
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: There is a quiet and costly irony unfolding in housing estates across Malaysia.
Families living in landed homes are paying private security guards to protect their streets, homes and children. They do so because they believe visible security is necessary. Yet on every ringgit they contribute towards this basic protection, they are also charged 8.0 per cent Service Tax.
This is a direct appeal to the Finance Minister. Exempt security and guard services paid by residents of landed housing estates from the Service Tax.
It is not a request for special treatment. It is a matter of fairness.
A COST OF FEELING SAFE
Guardhouses, boom gates, patrols and security cameras were once largely associated with high-rise residences and exclusive neighbourhoods. Today, they have become common in ordinary terrace housing areas.
Residents' associations, often led by unpaid volunteers, must negotiate with security companies, oversee payments, manage complaints and persuade neighbours to contribute. Many do this without statutory enforcement powers and while operating in neighbourhoods where roads remain public.
These residents are not buying a luxury service. They are pooling modest monthly contributions so that someone is present at the entrance, patrols the neighbourhood and responds when suspicious activity is spotted.
For a family contributing RM100 monthly, the 8.0 per cent SST adds RM8. That may appear small in isolation. But households already face mortgage payments, rent, school expenses, food costs, utility bills, assessment charges, road tax and insurance. Every additional charge matters, particularly when it is imposed on something as fundamental as personal safety.
Malaysia's general Service Tax rate rose from 6.0 per cent to 8.0 per cent on 1 March 2024. Guard and protection services for safety or security fall within the taxable service category.
The question is simple. Why should families be taxed when they are paying to secure the very places in which they live?
NOT A LUXURY
Security in a residential neighbourhood is not a premium lifestyle accessory. It is a practical response to real anxieties about theft, break-ins, scams, violence and the vulnerability of elderly residents and children.
Official statistics underline why these concerns cannot be brushed aside. Malaysia recorded 58,255 index crime cases in 2024, an 11.1 per cent increase over the preceding year. Property crime rose 12.4 per cent to 47,188 cases.
The figures do not mean every neighbourhood is unsafe. Nor should they be used to diminish the efforts of the Royal Malaysia Police. Police personnel work under demanding conditions, often with limited manpower, vast jurisdictions and an increasingly complex crime environment.
But the reality is that residents have turned to private security because they want an immediate and visible layer of protection. A guard at the entrance cannot replace the police. Neither can a residents' patrol investigate crime or bring offenders to justice. Yet they can deter opportunistic wrongdoing, alert authorities quickly and help create a safer environment.
This is community responsibility in action. It should be encouraged, not taxed.
A FAIR EXEMPTION
The government has shown that it recognises the need to protect the cost of living through targeted tax measures. Essential goods, including rice, chicken, vegetables and medicines, remain exempt from SST, while residential construction materials were excluded from the widened sales tax scope in the interest of affordability.
The same principle should apply to residential security services.
An exemption should be narrowly designed. It should apply to guard and protection services paid collectively by residents of landed, non-strata housing estates for the safety of their own neighbourhood. It need not extend to commercial premises, luxury clubs, private events or corporate security arrangements.
Such a policy would be clear, targeted and compassionate. It would recognise that a residents' association collecting funds for a night guard is not operating a business. It is a community trying to protect itself.
The Finance Ministry can work with the Royal Malaysian Customs Department, local authorities, the Home Ministry and registered residents' associations to establish a workable mechanism. Security firms should be required to identify exempt residential services separately on invoices. Associations should provide basic documentation showing that the service is funded by residents for a residential area.
This is administratively possible if the will exists.
REINFORCE PUBLIC SAFETY
Tax relief alone is not the answer. It must be accompanied by stronger and more visible policing.
Police stations must remain accessible to the public. Reporting crime should not become an exhausting journey across districts or a process that discourages victims from coming forward. Neighbourhood police posts must be properly supported, connected to patrol resources and equipped to deliver a meaningful frontline presence.
There should also be stronger coordination among the police, local councils, Rukun Tetangga groups and residents' associations. Community security cannot become a substitute for public policing. It should complement it.
The government must also publish district-level crime and response data. Communities deserve to know where the gaps are, where resources are most needed and how quickly calls for help are being answered.
THE RIGHT SIGNAL
Malaysia asks its people to be responsible citizens. Residents are responding by organising their communities, contributing their own money and working together to keep their neighbourhoods safe.
They should not be penalised for it.
An SST exemption for residential security services will not solve every concern about crime. But it will send a powerful message that the government understands the pressures faced by ordinary households living in landed properties.
Mr Finance Minister, security is not a luxury. Safety is not an optional extra. Families who pay to protect their homes should not be taxed for doing what they feel compelled to do.
Lift the SST on residential security services. It is fair, timely and necessary.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Fadhlina urges victims in freelance speaker case to lodge reports
Article:
ALOR GAJAH: The Education Ministry has urged victims in the case involving a freelance speaker accused of inappropriate conduct to come forward and lodge reports with the authorities to facilitate investigations.
Education Minister Datuk Seri Fadhlina Sidek said such reports were crucial to enable the authorities to investigate the allegations and allow the ministry to take appropriate action through established procedures.

Fadhlina added that the ministry takes the issue seriously and will not compromise on child safety in schools.

freelance speaker
accused of inappropriate behaviour to be stopped immediately to allow for a full investigation.

Title: Beware of ticket touts cashing in on F1, MotoGP, says Fuziah
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The public should remain vigilant against ticket touts seeking to cash in on several world-class events being held in Malaysia throughout October.
Deputy Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Dr Fuziah Salleh said Malaysia would host several international events this month, including the Gulf Air Bahrain Formula 1 (F1) Grand Prix Malaysia 2026, which begins tomorrow.
She said MotoGP is also expected to take place at the end of the month, with many people looking forward to experiencing the international motorsport event firsthand.
"I understand the public's excitement, and some may even have been saving up in anticipation of this elite motorsport event, but do not let that excitement allow ticket touts to make huge profits by offering tickets at exorbitant prices.
"More worryingly, purchasing tickets through unofficial sellers could expose us to scams. Not only would we have to pay a high price, but the tickets could also be invalid, leaving us to bear the losses," she said in a Facebook post.
Fuziah reminded the public to check the organiser's official channels and terms of purchase before making any payment, and not to trust screenshots or advertisements from unofficial sources.
"My advice is, let us return with sweet memories, rather than the regret of being scammed.
"Use our power as consumers by purchasing tickets through official channels to avoid becoming victims of ticket touting scams," she said.

Title: Homeowners in UK and beyond hit as global bond selloff drives up mortgage costs
Article:
LONDON: For five years, the interest rate on Richard Merrett's mortgage was locked at 1.14 per cent, but with that ultra-cheap deal due to expire in early 2027 he faces a sudden trebling of his monthly housing costs from £550 (US$728) a month to £1,650.
Merrett is no stranger to the risks in the lending market — he is managing director at mortgage firm Alexander Hall. But even he has been shocked by the scale of the increase, which has been stoked by a surge in energy prices caused by the Iran war.
"It's a big jump up and it means that the monthly payments are trebling. So there'll be some sharp intakes of breath and some belt-tightening," Merrett told Reuters.
A global bond market selloff has propelled borrowing costs from the US to Japan to decade highs and is impacting Britain's mortgage market, which could feed through to the wider economy.
It is also a harbinger of what could happen in the euro zone, the US and beyond if rates remain stubbornly high.
BORROWERS FACE MOUNTING PRESSURES
The rise in Britain's 30-year government bond yield , which topped 6.0 per cent on Thursday for the first time since 1998, will further increase mortgage rates as banks pass on the increased cost of funding to homebuyers, said Nicholas Mendes, mortgage manager at broker John Charcol.
"For borrowers, today's moves add to pressure that has been building for weeks," he said.
The 30-year yield stood just below 6.0 per cent on Friday.
Unlike in much of Europe and the US, where fixed-rate mortgages are typically funded via multi-decade loans, in Britain they are usually priced from two- and five-year swap rates.
The Bank of England in July estimated that over five million households were projected to see their mortgage repayments increase by end-2028, more than 1 million more than it expected before the start of the conflict in the Gulf.
For a typical homeowner, monthly mortgage repayments were projected to increase by a relatively manageable £45.
But for almost 750,000 people such as Merrett, who took out fixed-rate mortgages before rates began rising in 2022 from their Covid-era lows and which are due to expire this year, the average increase is £170 per month, the BoE estimated.
Mendes at John Charcol said Britain's two-year Sonia swap rate has risen 27 basis points in the last month to 4.68 per cent.
"That adds around a third of a percentage point to the cost of funding a fixed rate, and lenders cannot absorb that for long," he said.
Shortly after the start of the Iran war British banks withdrew more home loan products than on any day since the 2022 mini-budget crisis under then-Prime Minister Liz Truss. Lenders have been pulling sub-5.0 per cent deals in recent days.
GLOBAL PHENOMENON
Mortgage rates around the world are rising.
The US rate on a 30-year fixed-rate mortgage has soared more than 100 basis points since the war started and this week hit 7.28 per cent, its highest in almost three years, dealing another blow to first-time buyers. The week-on-week increase — the 30-year rate was 7.03 per cent last week — was the biggest in about four years.
In the euro area, loans with an initial fixed-rate period of 10 years-plus rose by 8 basis points to 3.43 per cent in August. The surge in euro zone government yields in recent weeks will push rates even higher.
In Australia, home prices fell for a sixth straight month in September, on track for the worst downturn in three decades.
In Britain, house prices last month rose at their weakest pace since December 2025, Nationwide Building Society said on Thursday, reflecting worries about possible Bank of England rate hikes.
MORTGAGE APPROVALS FALL
Data published this week showed the lowest number of UK mortgage approvals since the end of 2023, another sign of how rising borrowing costs are hitting demand.
Ashley Webb, senior UK economist at consultancy Capital Economics, said he still expected UK house prices to rise by 2.5 per cent in 2027, amid a lack of homes being put up for sale.
But the possibility of another jump in government borrowing in finance minister John Healey's first budget on October 28 could put more pressure on borrowing costs and "limit the housing recovery", Webb said.
For Merrett, the UK mortgage broker, the feeling is one of helplessness without the prospect of an end to the Iran war and no let-up in inflation pressures.
"I am worried. Why wouldn't you be when mortgage costs are trebling?" Merrett said. "But I remain quietly optimistic that we'll see some correction and things come down."

Title: Immigration turns up the heat on tomyam restaurants
Article:
KOTA BARU: The Immigration Department will step up enforcement at tomyam restaurants, including in Kelantan, following a claim by Thai authorities that about 100,000 workers at such eateries in Malaysia do not have valid work permits.
Immigration director-general Datuk Zakaria Shaaban said the department took note of the claim.
"Based on the department's records, as of Sept 15, there were 12,629 active Temporary Employment Visit Passes (PLKS) under the restaurant category.
"The department will not compromise and will take firm action against any foreigner who commits an immigration offence or abuses their pass to work or conduct any unauthorised business activities," he said.
He said they would strengthen enforcement to ensure foreign workers complied with the conditions of their passes and immigration laws.
His statement follows a claim by Thai authorities that about 100,000 workers at tomyam restaurants in Malaysia were working without valid permits.
According to an Utusan Malaysia report, Acting secretary-general of Thailand's Southern Border Provinces Administrative Centre (SBPAC), Chonthanya Saengphum, reportedly said there were about 200,000 Thai nationals working at some 5,000 tomyam restaurants in Malaysia.
He claimed more than half of them did not have valid work permits.
The issue has attracted attention as many Thai nationals work in the restaurant sector, particularly in states bordering Thailand, including Kelantan.

Title: Lorry driver jailed 11 years for killing man over wife lookalike remark
Article:
TAIPING: A lorry driver who caused the death of an acquaintance after the man spoke about having sex with a woman who resembled his wife was sentenced to 11 years in jail by the High Court.
B. Satiasarma, 41, and the victim, S. Sarathi, 20, had gone to a drug-taking spot at a palm oil plantation in Simpang Halt, near here, on April 30 last year.
According to the grounds of judgment by High Court judicial commissioner Syed Faisal Syed Amir, Satiasarma had heard a rumour that Sarathi was having an affair with his wife.
While they were at the location, Sarathi told Satiasarma that he had had sex with a woman whose characteristics were similar to those of Satiasarma's wife.
The remark caused Satiasarma to lose control and attack Sarathi with a knife, slashing his neck and stabbing him several times in the back.
The incident took place between 1.30pm and 2.30pm on April 30.
Sarathi was later found lying face down, covered in blood and partly concealed by branches beside a drain near a yellow scooter.
A post-mortem found that the cause of death was an incised wound to the neck with multiple stab wounds.
Police arrested Satiasarma about 11am the following day at a house in Taman Tekkah Permai.
About an hour later, he led police to a scrub area near a house in Jalan Utama Kampung Sungai Relong, Kamunting, where he pointed out where he had discarded the knife.
Police recovered an unbranded knife measuring about 23.2cm from the area.
Satiasarma had initially been charged with murder under Section 302 of the Penal Code.
However, on July 15 this year, the charge was amended to an alternative charge under Section 304(a) of the same Code, which covers culpable homicide not amounting to murder, to which he pleaded guilty.
In mitigation, he told the court that he was married with three sons and was the family's sole breadwinner, earning RM1,500 a month as a lorry driver.
He said his wife, who was a housewife, took up cleaning work earning RM1,500 a month after his arrest to support the family.
He expressed remorse and said his time in remand since May 1 last year had taught him to become a better person.
He asked the court to impose a minimum jail term, saying he wanted to return to his family, lead a normal life and care for his children.
The court was also referred to several previous Section 304(a) cases in which the sentences imposed ranged from eight to 11 years in jail.
Syed Faisal said the court had considered the mitigation, public interest, the accused's guilty plea and the sentencing trend.
"This case was not one involving a planned killing, but an incident that occurred suddenly and 'on the spur of the moment', with Sarathi's remark also contributing to the circumstances leading to the fatal attack.
"The court also took into account that Satiasarma had no previous convictions.
"This court finds that 11 years' jail from his arrest on May 1, 2025, is fair and proportionate to the offence," he said.
Deputy public prosecutor Sally Chay Mei Ling prosecuted, while lawyer Muhammad Hasif Hasan represented Satiasarma.
Chay urged the court to impose an appropriate sentence, saying that the punishment should serve as a lesson to the accused and that public interest should be prioritised.
She submitted that the sentencing trend for offences under Section 304(a) was between 15 and 20 years in jail.
She argued that Parliament's 2003 amendment increasing the maximum punishment for Section 304(a) offences from 20 to 30 years reflected the intention to impose a heavier punishment for offences involving the taking of a person's life.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Jobless man charged with misappropriating RM2,783 from customer
Article:
JOHOR BARU: An unemployed man was charged in the magistrate's court here today with misappropriating RM2,783.90 belonging to a customer of a money-changing company in March.
C. Narendran, 35, pleaded not guilty after the charge was read out to him before magistrate A. Shaarmini.
According to the charge, Narendran was accused of dishonestly converting RM2,783.90 belonging to a 32-year-old woman to his own use.
The offence was allegedly committed at a money changer's premises at Jalan Dedap 13, Taman Johor Jaya, here, at 1.17pm on March 9.

The court allowed him bail of RM7,000 with one surety and set Oct 16 for mention of the case and appointment of a lawyer.

Title: Proton blows past 2025 sales in nine months
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Proton Holdings Bhd has surpassed its full-year 2025 sales target in just nine months, with year-to-date (YTD) sales reaching 160,886 units as of September.
Proton said September sales rose 45 per cent year-on-year to 19,465 units, bringing YTD sales growth to 40.8 per cent.
The September performance also lifted Proton's estimated market share to 28.9 per cent, while its YTD market share stood at 26.9 per cent.
"This is the earliest sales have exceeded the 150,000 units barrier since 2002, the highest volume achieved since the partnership with Geely began in 2017.
"This means the company has beaten its total sales volume of 157,976 units from 2025 in just nine months," the carmaker said.
Proton Saga was the company's top-selling model in September, with 8,701 units delivered, bringing its YTD sales to 68,237 units, up 34.5 per cent from a year earlier.
Meanwhile, Proton S70 sales stood at 2,756 units in September, taking its YTD total to 20,709 units and surpassing its full-year 2025 sales.
Proton X50 remained the leader in the B-segment SUV category with YTD sales of 20,163 units, while X90 sales rose 69.8 per cent year-on-year to 3,250 units in the first nine months.
Proton deputy chief executive officer Datuk Abdul Rashid Musa said the company also recorded its best third-quarter performance since 2009, with 60,540 units sold.
"We still have at least two more launches to come before the end of the year, while our export business is targeting further growth in sales of both Proton and Geely badged vehicles originated from Malaysia, in overseas markets," he said.
Meanwhile, Proton's electrified vehicle arm Pro-Net has delivered 40,000 Proton e.Mas xEV units since sales began 20 months ago.
Pro-Net chief executive officer Zhang Qiang said e.Mas models now accounted for 19.3 per cent of Proton's overall sales, bringing the group close to the government's 2030 target for xEVs to account for 20 per cent of industry sales.
On exports, the national car company shipped 1,311 Proton and Geely vehicles from its Tanjung Malim plant in September, bringing total exports for the year to 7,370 units.

Title: HKL emergency dept upgrade enters final phase, completion targeted by end-2026
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 2 — The upgrading project of the new block of the Emergency and Trauma Department at the Kuala Lumpur Hospital (HKL) is now in the final phase of implementation.
The HKL Management said today that several issues require repair and improvement work in the inspection and completion process before the facility can be fully completed.
